topics.topic: How the runner receives its scratch-limit configuration
questions: Must RunnerLaunch gain a scratch-limit field, must the removed release scratch constant be restored and passed another way, or must the requirement that the limit travels in the runner's configuration change?

quotes: resource_exhausted when the report's resource_hit is true — the runner hit its memory, process or scratch limit, the scratch limit being the release's, which travels in the runner's configuration and not in ResourceBounds —, the observation's channel_over_bound holds, or the output count exceeds bounds.output_bytes;
RunnerLaunch fields (exact, no others exist): exchange_directory: str, code_file: str, inputs: tuple[RunnerInput, ...], output_ports: tuple[Port, ...], bounds: ResourceBounds, channel_fd: int
judgement.why: The requirement says the release scratch limit travels in the runner's configuration outside ResourceBounds, while the exact RunnerLaunch configuration model has no field that can carry it.

topics.topic: When the parent must terminate an environment
questions: Must the parent kill the environment when the channel exceeds its bound, or may it kill an environment only for its wall deadline?

quotes: when the runner writes more it stops reading, kills the environment as for its wall deadline, decodes what it read and observes channel_over_bound, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted.
the parent kills an environment for its wall deadline alone (owner, 2026-10-06).
judgement.why: One passage requires killing the environment when the channel exceeds its bound, while the other says the parent kills an environment only for its wall deadline.

topics.topic: Schema used for an extracted StoredValue delivered from a ListElementSource to a many receiving port
questions: For a many receiving port, must the extracted StoredValue use the port's value_schema directly, or the canonical array schema with that value_schema as items?

quotes: a ListElementSource first makes its list written as that list's own source says, then over a StoredValuesRef takes the element at map_index of the JSON array its StoredValue holds (read_value_bytes) as its own StoredValue of the receiving port's value_schema and the list's class
judgement.why: The ListElementSource requirement explicitly assigns the extracted StoredValue the receiving port's value_schema.

topics.topic: How plan_run should obtain JSON bytes for a StoredValue
questions: Must StoredValue gain a field containing the JSON bytes, or must the note say to construct an appropriate ByteSource from its value_id before calling read_value_bytes?

quotes: A mapped node's elements are the positions of a non-empty list delivered to its map_over port, counted from the JSON array its StoredValue holds — read with read_value_bytes, or the canonical_json of an AssembledList not yet written — or the files of its SpooledFilesRef;
StoredValue fields (exact, no others exist): value_id: str, value_digest: str, carriage: Carriage, media_type: str | None, value_schema: str, disclosure_class: DisclosureClass, size_bytes: int
StoredValueSource fields (exact, no others exist): source_kind: Literal['stored_value'], value_id: str
judgement.why: The requirement says to read a StoredValue with a function whose contract accepts ByteSource, while StoredValue has neither bytes nor a declared ByteSource relationship and the separate StoredValueSource is not named as the required argument.

topics.topic: Whether Run.inputs must be StoredValuesRef or plan_run must preserve arbitrary PortRef sources
questions: Must Run.inputs be restricted to StoredValuesRef, or must plan_run preserve any permitted PortRef when constructing a RecordedSource?
Must Run.inputs be restricted to StoredValuesRef, or must a direct flow-output source use the input's declared PortRef?

quotes: Run fields (exact, no others exist): run_id: str, flow_version_id: str, pinned_implementations: tuple[PinnedImplementation, ...], inputs: tuple[PortRef, ...], outputs: tuple[PortRef, ...], status: RunStatus, cancelled_by: Actor | None, waiting: tuple[WaitingPoint, ...], started_by: Actor, started_at: KernelInstant, ended_at: KernelInstant | None, resumptions: tuple[Resumption, ...], released_by: Actor | None, released_at: KernelInstant | None

Each element's sources are one per input port in port name order: a RecordedSource for a flow input's StoredValuesRef, a constant's StoredValuesRef or the output ref of an unmapped succeeded node on the enabled edge — from its NodeExecution or its ElementSucceeded outputs —;
A flow output's source is formed the same way; an output reached by an edge straight from a flow input is a RecordedSource of that input's StoredValuesRef (A13 rule 3).
judgement.why: The Run model permits inputs typed as PortRef, but both source-construction rules require every flow input to be a StoredValuesRef.
